changes: original_meaning 保留古英语 weorþ 的 gloss「有价值的，重要的」；该词更深来历不明（Boutkan 称无印欧词源）一节点入 mechanism_sentence 的口径，不入路径。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写入准介词化用法（约 1200 年，『相当于……的价值』）与名词『身家』义（1590 年代），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "worth (adj.) Middle English, from Old English weorþ \"having worth, significant, of value;\" also \"valued, appreciated, deserving; honorable, noble, of high rank;\" from Proto-Germanic *wertha-, which is of uncertain origin. Boutkan finds no IE etymology for it."
Etymonline: "It is attested from c. 1200 as a \"quasi-preposition\" [Middle English Compendium], \"equivalent to, of the value of, valued at; having importance equal to...\""
Etymonline: "worth (n.) Old English weorþ \"value of a commodity, monetary price, price paid...\" By 1590s as \"that which one is worth, wealth, riches, means, property.\""
worth.mechanism_sentence: worth 在古英语里一词两任：形容词是「有价值的」，名词是「价钱、价值」；约 1200 年它成了称量价值的准介词——值多少、值不值得，都拿它来量。它更深的来历，学界至今没有找到（Boutkan 语）。

semantic_path.how: 『有价值』长成了量价值的尺子：约 1200 年 worth 用作准介词——『相当于……的价值、抵得上……』（worth five pounds 值五英镑，be worth doing 值得做）；名词一支 1590 年代添『（人的）身家、净资产』义。词库『值得；价值』正分属这两支。

changes: original_meaning 大改：现行字段「脚背」取的是同源词的义（古诺斯语 rist『脚背』、德语 Rist『手背、脚背』），古英语 wrist 本词自始即指手与前臂之间的关节（Etymonline 明载）。改按本词 gloss 记录为「手腕」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 以『能转的关节』的语义理据与同源分工的事实充实，并记 wrist-watch 的年代（1889 年）。
evidence: Etymonline: "wrist (n.) \"joint of the body that connects the hand to the forearm,\" Old English wrist, from Proto-Germanic *wristiz (source also of Old Norse rist \"instep,\" Old Frisian wrist, Middle Dutch wrist, German Rist \"back of the hand, instep\"), from *wreik- \"to turn,\" which according to Watkins is from PIE root *wer- (2) \"to turn, bend.\" The notion is \"the turning joint.\""
Etymonline: "Wrist-watch, small watch worn on a band around the wrist, is attested by 1889."
Oxford: "Old English, of Germanic origin, probably from the base of writhe."
wrist.mechanism_sentence: wrist 的得名理据是「能转的关节」（与 writhe 同根，词源是「转」）：手腕是手转动的轴。它的亲戚们在别的语言里选了别的「转弯处」——古诺斯语 rist、德语 Rist 指的是脚背。

semantic_path.how: 守恒的实据在搭配的更新：1570 年代 wrist-band 指衬着手腕的袖口部分，1889 年 wrist-watch 出现——手表一戴上手腕，这个关节在英语里的出镜率从此不同；词义本身千年未动。

changes: original_meaning 保留「蛋黄」（古英语 ġeolca 的见载义，核对无误）；本条属守恒词，补丁以核对型规格处理。
semantic_path 第二站 how 以构词理据（geolu『黄』+ 指小后缀 -ca）充实，替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为浅述式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "yolk (n.) yellow part of the interior of an egg, as distinguished from the white, Middle English yolke, from Old English geolca, geoloca \"yolk,\" etymologically \"the yellow part,\" from geolu \"yellow\" (see yellow (adj.)). Formerly also spelled yelk."
Wiktionary: "from Old English ġeolca, ġioleca 'the yellow part, yolk', derived from ġeolu 'yellow' + -ca, diminutive suffix."
yolk.mechanism_sentence: yolk 是个看颜色起的名字：古英语 ġeolca 就是「黄的那一小团」（geolu「黄」加上指小的 -ca）——蛋黄叫什么，一望而知。

semantic_path.how: 守恒的实据在构词的透明：ġeolca 自始至终指蛋里黄色的那部分，从未转移或分化（旧拼 yelk 曾与 yolke 并行）——词库今义即首站本义。

changes: original_meaning 保留古英语 ġeoguþ 的 gloss「年轻的状态；青年时期」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 补单指个人的年代（约 1200 年）与构词格式（young + 抽象后缀 -th），替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为浅述式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "youth (n.) Middle English, from Old English geoguð \"the early stage of life, youthfulness; young people, junior warriors; young of cattle,\" related to geong \"young,\" from Proto-Germanic *jugunthi- (from suffixed form of PIE root *yeu- \"vital force, youthful vigor\"; see young (adj.)) + Proto-Germanic abstract noun suffix *-itho (see -th (2))."
Etymonline: "As \"a young person,\" especially \"a young man,\" by c. 1200; in this sense it has a plural."
youth.mechanism_sentence: youth 是 young 加抽象后缀 -th 造出来的（与 health、width 一个格式）：古英语 ġeoguþ 指「年轻的这段时期、这群年轻人」，约 1200 年起也落到单个的青年人身上。

semantic_path.how: 抽象名词具体化：约 1200 年 youth 添『一个青年人（尤指小伙子）』义并有了复数——从一段时期、一群人，落到一个人身上；词库今义『青年；青春』双收，正分属新旧两站。
